study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Place value and magnitude in Number Sense & Estimation.
study_materials.teaching_content: Read, compose and compare whole numbers and decimals by place value; use powers of ten to explain magnitude.
worked_examples: Compare 4,080 and 4,008 by examining the hundreds and tens places.
study_materials.pitfall: A common error is treating 0 as having no structural role; in 4,080 it preserves the tens place.
study_materials.mastery_check: Estimate sums and products before calculating exactly; reject answers whose size is impossible.
study_materials.revision: Revise Place value and magnitude through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Rounding and estimation in Number Sense & Estimation.
study_materials.teaching_content: Round integers and decimals to stated place values and use estimation to predict reasonable answers.
worked_examples: Round 7,496 to the nearest hundred: 7,500 because the tens digit is 9.
study_materials.pitfall: When estimating 398×21, use 400×20=8,000 as a reasonableness benchmark.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use compatible numbers, bounds and reverse checks to verify numerical answers.
study_materials.revision: Revise Rounding and estimation through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Factors, multiples and primes in Number Sense & Estimation.
study_materials.teaching_content: Identify factors, multiples, primes, composite numbers, common factors and common multiples.
worked_examples: For 36, factor pairs are 1×36, 2×18, 3×12 and 4×9.
study_materials.pitfall: A number divisible by 6 must be divisible by both 2 and 3.
study_materials.mastery_check: Apply divisibility rules, prime factorisation, GCD and LCM in unfamiliar problems.
study_materials.revision: Revise Factors, multiples and primes through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Mental calculation strategies in Number Sense & Estimation.
study_materials.teaching_content: Choose efficient mental methods for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and percentage calculations.
worked_examples: Use 25×16 as 100÷4×16=400 rather than repeated addition.
study_materials.pitfall: Watch for carrying and place-value errors when splitting numbers mentally.
study_materials.mastery_check: Select a method, estimate first, calculate, then verify using an inverse operation.
study_materials.revision: Revise Mental calculation strategies through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Number properties and puzzles in Number Sense & Estimation.
study_materials.teaching_content: Use parity, divisibility, remainders and numerical structure to solve non-routine problems.
worked_examples: If an integer is odd, adding another odd integer produces an even result.
study_materials.pitfall: A remainder must be smaller than the divisor; this gives an immediate validity check.
study_materials.mastery_check: Combine parity and divisibility constraints to eliminate impossible cases before calculation.
study_materials.revision: Revise Number properties and puzzles through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Equivalent fractions and simplification in Fractions, Ratios & Proportion.
study_materials.teaching_content: Generate equivalent fractions, reduce fractions using common factors, and compare fractions reliably.
worked_examples: 3/4 and 9/12 represent the same quantity because both simplify to 3/4.
study_materials.pitfall: Do not compare denominators alone; convert to common denominators or benchmark against 1/2 and 1.
study_materials.mastery_check: Solve comparison and ordering problems involving mixed numbers and improper fractions.
study_materials.revision: Revise Equivalent fractions and simplification through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Fraction operations in Fractions, Ratios & Proportion.
study_materials.teaching_content: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions while explaining why each operation works.
worked_examples: For 2/3+1/6, rewrite 2/3 as 4/6, giving 5/6.
study_materials.pitfall: Division by a fraction asks how many groups of that size fit into the dividend.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use inverse operations and magnitude estimates to detect impossible fraction results.
study_materials.revision: Revise Fraction operations through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Ratios and equivalent ratios in Fractions, Ratios & Proportion.
study_materials.teaching_content: Interpret ratios as comparisons and scale them without changing the underlying relationship.
worked_examples: A 2:3 ratio becomes 8:12 when both parts are multiplied by 4.
study_materials.pitfall: A ratio is not automatically a fraction of the whole; distinguish comparison from total share.
study_materials.mastery_check: Solve missing-value, mixture and scale problems using tables, unit rates or equivalent ratios.
study_materials.revision: Revise Ratios and equivalent ratios through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Proportion and scaling in Fractions, Ratios & Proportion.
study_materials.teaching_content: Recognise proportional relationships and apply scale factors to quantities, diagrams and rates.
worked_examples: If 3 notebooks cost ₹90, the unit price is ₹30 and 7 cost ₹210 under the same rate.
study_materials.pitfall: A proportional relationship keeps the same multiplicative scale factor.
study_materials.mastery_check: Test whether a relationship is truly proportional before applying cross-multiplication.
study_materials.revision: Revise Proportion and scaling through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Percentages in context in Fractions, Ratios & Proportion.
study_materials.teaching_content: Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages and apply percentage change to real situations.
worked_examples: 15% of ₹800 is ₹120, so the discounted price is ₹680.
study_materials.pitfall: A 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease does not return to the starting value.
study_materials.mastery_check: Solve discount, tax, comparison and percentage-change problems with explicit base quantities.
study_materials.revision: Revise Percentages in context through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Variables and expressions in Algebraic Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Represent unknown quantities with variables and translate verbal descriptions into algebraic expressions.
worked_examples: Five more than x is x+5; five times x is 5x.
study_materials.pitfall: Do not confuse addition with multiplication when translating phrases.
study_materials.mastery_check: Evaluate expressions for given values and explain the role of each term.
study_materials.revision: Revise Variables and expressions through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Simplifying expressions in Algebraic Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Combine like terms and use distributive reasoning to simplify algebraic expressions.
worked_examples: 3x+5x becomes 8x because both terms contain the same variable quantity.
study_materials.pitfall: 2(x+3) means two groups of both x and 3, so it becomes 2x+6.
study_materials.mastery_check: Check simplification by substituting a numerical value for x before and after.
study_materials.revision: Revise Simplifying expressions through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Equations and unknowns in Algebraic Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Solve one- and multi-step equations while preserving equality.
worked_examples: For 3x+5=20, subtract 5 then divide by 3 to obtain x=5.
study_materials.pitfall: Performing the same operation on both sides preserves equality.
study_materials.mastery_check: Substitute the solution back into the original equation to verify it.
study_materials.revision: Revise Equations and unknowns through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Inequalities and constraints in Algebraic Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Interpret inequality symbols and solve simple constrained problems.
worked_examples: x>4 includes every number greater than 4, not 4 itself.
study_materials.pitfall: Boundary values determine whether an inequality is strict or inclusive.
study_materials.mastery_check: Translate word constraints into inequalities and test candidate values.
study_materials.revision: Revise Inequalities and constraints through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Algebraic word problems in Algebraic Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Build equations from real situations involving unknowns, rates, totals and comparisons.
worked_examples: If three equal notebooks and a ₹20 pen cost ₹140, represent the notebook price as x and solve 3x+20=140.
study_materials.pitfall: Identify the unknown and units before writing the equation.
study_materials.mastery_check: Check the solution against the original story, including units and non-negative constraints.
study_materials.revision: Revise Algebraic word problems through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Angles and relationships in Geometry & Measurement.
study_materials.teaching_content: Use straight-line, around-a-point, vertically opposite and triangle angle facts to determine unknown angles.
worked_examples: Angles on a straight line total 180°, so an angle of 127° leaves 53°.
study_materials.pitfall: Diagrams are not necessarily drawn to scale; use stated mathematical relationships.
study_materials.mastery_check: Combine multiple angle facts and verify the final angle against the geometry.
study_materials.revision: Revise Angles and relationships through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Perimeter and area in Geometry & Measurement.
study_materials.teaching_content: Calculate perimeter and area of standard and composite figures and distinguish the two measures.
worked_examples: An 8 cm by 5 cm rectangle has area 40 cm² and perimeter 26 cm.
study_materials.pitfall: Perimeter measures boundary length; area measures covered surface.
study_materials.mastery_check: Decompose composite figures and check units: cm for perimeter, cm² for area.
study_materials.revision: Revise Perimeter and area through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Triangles and polygons in Geometry & Measurement.
study_materials.teaching_content: Classify polygons and apply side and angle properties to solve problems.
worked_examples: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three 60° angles.
study_materials.pitfall: A quadrilateral has interior-angle sum 360°.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use known properties rather than visual appearance to justify classification.
study_materials.revision: Revise Triangles and polygons through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Volume and measurement in Geometry & Measurement.
study_materials.teaching_content: Calculate volume and convert length, area and volume units consistently.
worked_examples: A 4×3×2 cm cuboid has volume 24 cm³.
study_materials.pitfall: Area uses squared units and volume uses cubed units.
study_materials.mastery_check: Convert units before combining quantities and check dimensional consistency.
study_materials.revision: Revise Volume and measurement through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Coordinates and spatial reasoning in Geometry & Measurement.
study_materials.teaching_content: Plot and interpret coordinates and reason about movement, symmetry and position.
worked_examples: The point (3,-2) is three units right and two units below the origin.
study_materials.pitfall: The first coordinate is horizontal and the second vertical.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use coordinate changes and symmetry to solve unfamiliar spatial problems.
study_materials.revision: Revise Coordinates and spatial reasoning through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Arithmetic patterns in Patterns & Sequences.
study_materials.teaching_content: Identify constant differences and use them to predict later terms.
worked_examples: 4,7,10,13 has constant difference 3.
study_materials.pitfall: Do not infer a rule from only one transition.
study_materials.mastery_check: Represent the rule by position and verify it on several terms.
study_materials.revision: Revise Arithmetic patterns through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Geometric patterns in Patterns & Sequences.
study_materials.teaching_content: Recognise constant multiplicative change and distinguish it from additive change.
worked_examples: 2,6,18,54 multiplies by 3 each time.
study_materials.pitfall: A constant ratio differs from a constant difference.
study_materials.mastery_check: Test the ratio across consecutive terms before generalising.
study_materials.revision: Revise Geometric patterns through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Recursive rules in Patterns & Sequences.
study_materials.teaching_content: Describe how each term is generated from an earlier term.
worked_examples: In 2,5,8,11 each term is the previous term plus 3.
study_materials.pitfall: A recursive rule describes progression but may not directly give the nth term.
study_materials.mastery_check: Trace from the initial value and verify every generated term.
study_materials.revision: Revise Recursive rules through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Visual patterns in Patterns & Sequences.
study_materials.teaching_content: Translate growing diagrams into numerical relationships.
worked_examples: If each stage adds four tiles, stage totals can be modelled from that structural change.
study_materials.pitfall: Counting only an outer edge can miss repeated internal units.
study_materials.mastery_check: Make a stage-number table before proposing a general rule.
study_materials.revision: Revise Visual patterns through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Pattern-based reasoning in Patterns & Sequences.
study_materials.teaching_content: Use patterns to discover, test and justify general relationships.
worked_examples: Test small cases to expose a possible invariant before proving it.
study_materials.pitfall: A pattern seen in three cases is evidence, not proof.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use algebra, parity or structural reasoning to justify the generalisation.
study_materials.revision: Revise Pattern-based reasoning through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Tables and graphs in Data & Probability.
study_materials.teaching_content: Read values, scales, categories and trends accurately from common data displays.
worked_examples: Always inspect the axis scale before comparing bar heights.
study_materials.pitfall: A visual gap can exaggerate a numerical difference.
study_materials.mastery_check: Extract exact values before calculating or drawing conclusions.
study_materials.revision: Revise Tables and graphs through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Averages and spread in Data & Probability.
study_materials.teaching_content: Calculate and interpret mean, median, mode and range.
worked_examples: For 2,4,4,10 the mean is 5 while the median is 4.
study_materials.pitfall: Extreme values can move the mean substantially.
study_materials.mastery_check: Choose the statistic that matches the question and dataset.
study_materials.revision: Revise Averages and spread through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Basic probability in Data & Probability.
study_materials.teaching_content: Represent likelihood and calculate simple probabilities from defined sample spaces.
worked_examples: A fair die has probability 3/6=1/2 of producing an even number.
study_materials.pitfall: Probability lies from 0 to 1 inclusive.
study_materials.mastery_check: Define equally likely outcomes before forming the probability ratio.
study_materials.revision: Revise Basic probability through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Counting outcomes in Data & Probability.
study_materials.teaching_content: Systematically count possible outcomes without omissions or duplicates.
worked_examples: Two coin tosses have HH, HT, TH and TT when order matters.
study_materials.pitfall: HT and TH are different ordered outcomes.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use tables, lists or tree diagrams to make the sample space explicit.
study_materials.revision: Revise Counting outcomes through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Evidence from data in Data & Probability.
study_materials.teaching_content: Make conclusions supported by data while recognising limits.
worked_examples: A higher average does not mean every individual observation is higher.
study_materials.pitfall: A small association does not establish causation.
study_materials.mastery_check: State the evidence and avoid claims stronger than the dataset supports.
study_materials.revision: Revise Evidence from data through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Working backwards in Logical Problem Solving.
study_materials.teaching_content: Reverse a sequence of operations to recover an unknown starting value.
worked_examples: If doubling a number and adding 7 gives 31, subtract 7 then divide by 2.
study_materials.pitfall: Reverse operations in the opposite order from the original.
study_materials.mastery_check: Run the original process forward to verify the recovered value.
study_materials.revision: Revise Working backwards through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Systematic case analysis in Logical Problem Solving.
study_materials.teaching_content: Break constrained problems into complete, non-overlapping cases.
worked_examples: List possible integer values under each condition rather than guessing.
study_materials.pitfall: Overlapping cases can double-count solutions.
study_materials.mastery_check: Define cases and show that every valid possibility is included exactly once.
study_materials.revision: Revise Systematic case analysis through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Invariants and constraints in Logical Problem Solving.
study_materials.teaching_content: Identify properties that remain unchanged during a process.
worked_examples: A move may change token positions while preserving the total number of tokens.
study_materials.pitfall: A proposed final state violating an invariant is impossible.
study_materials.mastery_check: Test parity, totals, colour counts or other conserved quantities.
study_materials.revision: Revise Invariants and constraints through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Mathematical classification in Logical Problem Solving.
study_materials.teaching_content: Classify objects using explicit mathematical properties.
worked_examples: Even and odd are complementary integer classifications, while prime and composite concern factors.
study_materials.pitfall: A visual resemblance is not a mathematical classification rule.
study_materials.mastery_check: State the defining property and test it consistently.
study_materials.revision: Revise Mathematical classification through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Non-routine puzzles in Logical Problem Solving.
study_materials.teaching_content: Combine several ideas when no standard procedure is immediately obvious.
worked_examples: Try small cases, represent the structure, identify constraints and then generalise.
study_materials.pitfall: Blind trial-and-error can miss solutions.
study_materials.mastery_check: Record failed approaches and use them to narrow the remaining possibilities.
study_materials.revision: Revise Non-routine puzzles through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Translate language into mathematics in Multi-step Word Problems.
study_materials.teaching_content: Identify quantities, relationships, units and operations in written situations.
worked_examples: “Three times as many” represents multiplication by 3.
study_materials.pitfall: Separate essential quantities from decorative information.
study_materials.mastery_check: Write a short mathematical model before calculating.
study_materials.revision: Revise Translate language into mathematics through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Rates, time and distance in Multi-step Word Problems.
study_materials.teaching_content: Use speed, distance and time relationships with consistent units.
worked_examples: At 60 km/h for 2.5 hours, distance is 150 km.
study_materials.pitfall: Hours and minutes must be reconciled before applying a rate.
study_materials.mastery_check: Check both magnitude and unit of the result.
study_materials.revision: Revise Rates, time and distance through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Combined work rates in Multi-step Word Problems.
study_materials.teaching_content: Model jointly completed tasks by adding rates rather than completion times.
worked_examples: Rates of 1/4 and 1/6 job per hour combine to 5/12 job per hour.
study_materials.pitfall: Adding completion times reverses the relationship.
study_materials.mastery_check: Express each worker as a fraction of one job per unit time.
study_materials.revision: Revise Combined work rates through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Multi-operation problems in Multi-step Word Problems.
study_materials.teaching_content: Plan sequential operations while preserving units and the meaning of intermediate quantities.
worked_examples: A shopping problem may require discount, tax and final-total calculations in a specific order.
study_materials.pitfall: Applying a percentage to the wrong base can produce a plausible number.
study_materials.mastery_check: Annotate each intermediate result and compare it with the story.
study_materials.revision: Revise Multi-operation problems through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Solution verification in Multi-step Word Problems.
study_materials.teaching_content: Check a word-problem answer against every stated condition.
worked_examples: A fractional number of required whole objects can signal a modelling error.
study_materials.pitfall: A correct arithmetic result can still answer the wrong question.
study_materials.mastery_check: Substitute the result back into the situation and verify all constraints.
study_materials.revision: Revise Solution verification through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Efficient calculation in Speed, Accuracy & Verification.
study_materials.teaching_content: Choose valid transformations that reduce calculation without sacrificing exactness.
worked_examples: 48×25 can be evaluated as 48×100÷4=1200.
study_materials.pitfall: A shortcut is useful only when its transformation preserves the value.
study_materials.mastery_check: Compare with an estimate or inverse operation.
study_materials.revision: Revise Efficient calculation through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Estimation before exact work in Speed, Accuracy & Verification.
study_materials.teaching_content: Predict the scale and reasonable range of an answer before detailed calculation.
worked_examples: 198×51 should be near 200×50, or 10,000.
study_materials.pitfall: A result far outside the estimated range is immediately suspicious.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use upper and lower estimates to create a reasonableness band.
study_materials.revision: Revise Estimation before exact work through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Answer-choice elimination in Speed, Accuracy & Verification.
study_materials.teaching_content: Reject options using parity, magnitude, units and constraints.
worked_examples: If the exact answer must be even, odd choices can be eliminated with a reason.
study_materials.pitfall: Elimination is not guessing; each rejection requires evidence.
study_materials.mastery_check: Directly verify the remaining candidate.
study_materials.revision: Revise Answer-choice elimination through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Error classification in Speed, Accuracy & Verification.
study_materials.teaching_content: Distinguish interpretation, method, arithmetic and verification errors.
worked_examples: A copied digit error differs from choosing the wrong formula.
study_materials.pitfall: Changing only the final number may leave the misconception intact.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify the first incorrect step and repair it.
study_materials.revision: Revise Error classification through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of Timed mixed practice in Speed, Accuracy & Verification.
study_materials.teaching_content: Balance speed with accuracy across unfamiliar mathematics problems.
worked_examples: Allocate time by difficulty and return to marked questions.
study_materials.pitfall: Rushing increases avoidable reading and arithmetic errors.
study_materials.mastery_check: Track accuracy, skipped questions and error types after each timed set.
study_materials.revision: Revise Timed mixed practice through worked examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

mock_tests.focus: number, ratio, algebra and geometry foundations
patterns, data, probability and multi-step reasoning
